node_definition.done_when: Read the plan section with read_plan(view='section', section='s2') before starting; it is the authority. The followup's invocation is its prompt field, with recommends_skill as the fallback, in the grammar /reckon-VERB TARGET optionally followed by a section sign and a number. TARGET is a bare slug, project:slug or a sprint id. The section number maps to the section id s plus that number. A followup is a pointer when TARGET names a plan other than its host, a plan in another mount, or a sprint, or when it names its host plan together with a section that the host's section_declarations classify implementable. Anything else hides work, with a reason word from a fixed set that distinguishes no-section, section-not-implementable, host-complete and unparseable. The roadmap finding is emitted next to _unwired_plan_findings in reckon/roadmap.py through the existing _finding helper. It covers every plan the roadmap inventories, including completed ones, and names the plan, the followup id and the reason word. No other module re-implements the classification. In a new tests/test_a_followup_that_hides_work_is_found.py, built on plans written into a temporary docs directory (never the real docs tree or configuration home), assert the predicate's answer and reason for five cases: a pointer to another plan, a pointer to the host's implementable section, a followup naming a done section, a followup naming no section, and a followup on a shipped plan naming its host. Assert also that the roadmap's findings list exactly the three that hide work. Execute the named negative control and confirm the no-section case fails. Then run the predicate over the real /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/docs/plans read-only and write a log in the run directory with the count by reason word, plus every followup id the plan's section 1 counted as hiding work (102 rows) that the predicate calls a pointer, or the reverse, each with its reason. The gate is the new test plus every existing test file under tests/ that imports reckon.roadmap or calls roadmap(, found by a text search; run it at base and at head and list the files in the manifest. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. Every pytest process uses a basetemp private to that process, outside any repository. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/work-is-a-section-not-a-followup/predicate-and-finding.html records the change, the real-tree counts and the disagreements. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: Land section 2 of work-is-a-section-not-a-followup as the plan states it: one predicate in a new module reckon/followup_pointers.py classifies an open followup as a pointer or as hiding work, with a fixed reason word, and the roadmap reports every open followup that hides work as a warn-severity wiring finding built on that same predicate.
